gpt.text:
To continue from this handoff, you can run the three “Next Commands” exactly as listed; they form a sensible pipeline: (1) pick best module-level candidate, (2) run system-level candidates, (3) generate the next targeted fix report.

## What each command will do (and what to look for)

1) **AUB autopilot (module-level)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
- Runs the AUB/module experiments defined in `module_registry.yaml`.
- `--select-best` typically updates whatever “best” pointer or output artifact your framework uses (often by writing a new candidate/champion file or updating a registry entry).
- After it finishes, check:
  - Which module/version it selected as “best”
  - Any updated JSON artifacts under `baseline/` (or wherever your framework writes winners)
  - Whether it produced a PASS candidate (your handoff says none last time)

2) **System autopilot (end-to-end)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
- Runs end-to-end/system candidates from `system_candidates.yaml`.
- This is where you validate that the module-level win actually improves the full system and doesn’t regress other metrics.
- After it finishes, check:
  - Whether any system candidate beats `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
  - Any regressions vs the champion on the tracked metrics (you posted tuning_mean/min and lockbox_mean/min; confirm which metric is the actual selection criterion)

3) **Next fix generator (triage / action plan)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
- Produces a “what to fix next” report based on the latest run results and registry state.
- Open `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` and use it to decide the next targeted change if no clear winner emerges.

## Recommended run order
Run them in the same order given. If (1) selects a new best module, (2) will test it in realistic conditions; (3) then summarizes gaps.

## Quick sanity checks before you run
- Ensure the “current champion” file exists: `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- Confirm you have write permission to `baseline/` and `baseline/reports/`
- If your tooling supports it, capture logs to files for later diffing (e.g., `... | tee baseline/logs/...`)

## If you paste results, I can help decide the winner
If you share the stdout summaries (or the produced report files), I can help interpret:
- whether “tuning_mean/min” and “lockbox_mean/min” are “higher is better” vs “lower is better,”
- whether the improvements are statistically/meaningfully significant,
- and whether you should promote a new champion or generate a targeted fix.
